text:
Anna: heads up — nightly bench fired an alert on the apples-to-apples harness: large variance in p50/p95 after the kernel-selector change. kv-cache warmup looks inconsistent. anyone on this?
perf-bot: [ALERT] 1893002468 - apples-a2a-nightly - p95 regression 18% vs baseline. payload: kernels=[fused_attn_v2,attn_opt], seeds=auto, runs=50. dashboard: https://perf.redwood.internal/d/bench/ApplesToApples
Josh: saw this too. Replay vs synthetic diverge after the last kernel selector tweak (commit 5c9a2). replay shows slower p95, synthetic stable.
Priya: I did a quick local replay with the nightly harness and can repro variance. Key is KV cache cold-start on some traces — first few steps balloon latencies. seq_len=1024, batch=1 reproduces.
Liam: is kernel auto-selection flipping between fused_attn_v2 and attn_opt during the run? That could explain inconsistent perf profiles.
Priya: yes — the selector heuristic introduced a tiny perf delta and it flips when estimated flop count is borderline. CI harness currently lets selector run per-inference.
Anna: options: (1) force a deterministic kernel in CI apples-to-apples so we measure apples-to-apples, (2) add warmup iterations for KV cache, (3) loosen alert thresholds while we triage. Prefer forcing determinism + warmup.
Josh: agreed on forcing determinism. Also propose we record the kernel chosen per-run in the dashboard so diffs show kernel distribution.
Priya: putting a minimal config tweak here that reproduced the stable run locally:
```yaml
harness:
  mode: replay
  kernel_override: fused_attn_v2
  kv_warmup_iters: 3
  runs: 40
  seed: 42
```
Priya: with that config p95 lines up with baseline within 2%. Without kernel_override + no warmup, p95 diverged ~18%.
Liam: for CI automation: we should add a small pre-warm step to the nightly job that runs 3 synthetic warmup traces per kernel. That won't add much cost but will stabilize KV behavior.
Anna: also we need a flaky test process note: if nightly shows regression but kernel distribution changed, mark as "kernel-selector-variance" and auto-mute alert for 24h so humans can triage instead of pager storms. perf-bot, can we add a mute action?
perf-bot: action taken: muted alert apples-a2a-nightly for 24h (reason: triage in-progress). Added annotation tag: kernel-selector-variance.
Josh: I'll open a dashboard card that shows kernel selection histogram + kv warmup traces next to latency percentiles. link once created.
Priya: I'll draft a small PR to the harness to (a) add kernel_override option for CI apples-to-apples, (b) add kv_warmup_iters default=3, (c) log kernel per-run to s3. Assigning to Liam for review.
Liam: assigned, will review this afternoon. Also propose follow-up: add replay-vs-synth nightly comparison and publish the delta to a separate panel.
Anna: perfect. Priya — estimated time?
Priya: small PR, ~2-3 hours + tests. I'll also add a short note in the perf runbook about how to interpret kernel-selector-variance tag.
Josh: thx. once PR lands, let's re-run the apples-to-apples job manually to confirm.
Anna: good plan. marking triage owner = Priya, reviewer = Liam. will revisit tomorrow during standup. :thumbsup:
